slop.quote: New reps are only as effective as the list they're handed on day one.

slop.pattern: padding before the ask (soft pitch phrasing)
slop.quote: I'd like to walk you through how we did it and what a rebuilt list could look like for Kova.

unsupported: "If your Malaysia team is about to start prospecting APAC SMBs" assumes timing and target (hedged as a conditional, so minor)
compliance_issues: First two lines are the job-post hook plus a generic aphorism. Neither says why Deep is writing, and the ask comes in the last line

unsupported: Subject says "SDR hires" but the brief says openings (minor)
compliance_issues: None. 64 words, all three facts used, ask present. Line 2 states the purpose. It could tie the bounce result to Kova a little more explicitly

B1_cold_email.why: B says who, why and what in 64 plain words with no aphorism, while A pads with a portable maxim and a walk-you-through line that makes the ask feel like a pitch.

slop.pattern: binary contrast (X doesn't fail because of Y)
slop.quote: Most AI SDR pilots don't fail because of the AI.
Each one had the same complaint: the agent was sending, but the replies weren't coming.
The problem wasn't the prompts, the sequences, or the model.
People who had left the company. Addresses that bounced.

slop.pattern: robotic parallel pair plus empty adverb
slop.quote: The agents were doing exactly what they were told. They were just doing it to people who weren't there anymore.
An AI SDR scales whatever you feed it.
Give it a clean list and it scales conversations. Give it a stale one and it scales bounces
audit the list before you audit the agent.

unsupported: "Each one had the same complaint: the agent was sending, but the replies weren't coming" is an invented client complaint
"The problem wasn't the prompts, the sequences, or the model" presents unverified reasoning as fact
"leadership walks away convinced AI outbound doesn't work" is an invented outcome
"Most AI SDR pilots" generalizes from an audit of 3 pilots
compliance_issues: 160 words, inside range. The opening line is a binary-contrast hook rather than the finding, so the data doesn't show up until line 2

slop.quote: In all 3, the agents were working from stale lists. ... Reply rates roughly doubled in all 3 pilots.

unsupported: "More than a third of each list" turns an aggregate 38% into a per-list claim the brief does not support
"every one of those contacts still counted against the pilot's reply rate" is inferred reasoning presented as fact
"In all 3, the agents were working from stale lists" is a slight stretch from the brief, which gives only an overall 38% figure
compliance_issues: None. 138 words, and the first two lines carry the audit and the finding. It ends on a real question

B2_linkedin_post.why: B leads with the audit data and reasons plainly, while A is a stack of LinkedIn tics (binary hook, fragments, parallel pairs, chiasmus kicker) wrapped around invented color.

slop.quote: Your HCP database was accurate the day it was built. It probably isn't today.
They join a new group, move to a hospital system, split time across clinics, or leave a practice altogether.
The name is still right. The specialty is still right. But the clinic your rep is driving to is one the physician no longer works at.
That's a cost most pharma marketing teams never see on a dashboard: a rep in the wrong waiting room, a visit that doesn't happen, a planned conversation that never takes place.
stale affiliation data stops being a data problem. It becomes a field-force problem.
Here's why HCP data decays so quickly, and what your team can do about it.
Each move quietly breaks a record in your CRM.

unsupported: "was accurate the day it was built"
"a cost most pharma marketing teams never see on a dashboard" is an unsourced generalization
"split time across clinics, or leave a practice altogether" goes past the brief's plain affiliation change
"decays so quickly" implies a rate the brief does not quantify
compliance_issues: About 155 words of body plus the title, slightly over 150
Ends on a metadiscourse transition instead of a concrete point

slop.quote: The visit is lost, and so is the rep's time.
The affiliation is the part that went wrong, and it is the part that tells a rep where to go.
A record can pass every other test and still send a rep to the wrong clinic.

unsupported: "nobody flags the record" is an assertion without support
"a steady stream of records" is inferred from 'often' with no number (reasonable, but still reasoning presented as fact)
"the first field to check" is opinion presented as fact (acceptable for a blog voice)
compliance_issues: None. Exactly 150 words, no invented statistics, the opening scene carries the message, and both Ampliz numbers are used

B3_blog_intro.why: B opens on a concrete field scene and stays inside the facts, while A strings a colon-reveal tricolon, a stops-being/becomes turn and a Here's-why transition around claims the brief doesn't support.

unsupported: "The CFO of a logistics firm" where the brief says "a CFO" (trivial)
compliance_issues: None. The subject and the first two lines carry both the status and the deadline ask, it is short and plain, and it names no vendor
